A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSA research work and contain 21 readable pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–J. The material supports comparison despite table relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original MSA experiments on TOFU, RESTOR and MUSE-Books, plus checkpoint-selection, repeated-exposure and judge-validation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses, including their numerical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same checkpoint-based forget-vector construction, optional retain vector, retain-data subsampling and weighted parameter update. The revised framework diagram does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use TOFU, RESTOR and MUSE-Books with the same task coverage. The TOFU–C4 and TOFU–C4–TOFU scenarios highlighted in v3 already appear in v2 Appendices F and G.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator membership, including the reported subsets of NPO, RMU, GradDiff, Task Vector, SatImp and UNDIAL. Table 12 retains the same checkpoint-augmented baselines; reference-row renaming introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: Models, checkpoints, metrics, training budgets and hyperparameter searches remain unchanged. Appendices C–E retain the same validation splits, including 15% for TOFU/MUSE-Books and 10% for RESTOR. v3's main-text C4 scenario description matches the existing appendix protocol.

E4.justification: Checkpoint-distance comparisons, qualitative metric examples, human validation of the judge, intervening C4 training, repeated exposure and checkpoint-augmented baseline analyses all exist in both versions. v3 adds main-text summaries and relocates an existing table without introducing another analysis.

E5.justification: Run/seed information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including the 200-judgment human audit reporting 96% agreement. The revised Forget Quality value is a numerical result change, not a change in statistical procedure.

E6.justification: For TOFU followed by C4, the ideal row changes from v2 Table 10 to v3 Table 5: Accrecover rises from 0.45 to 0.98 and Forget Quality from 1.31e-04 to 1. In the repeated-exposure experiment, Table 11's ideal Accrecover changes from 0.52 to 0.98. Unlearning-method scores and other table values remain unchanged; the reference-score revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, parameter-update equations, validation-score formulas and Appendix H adaptation equation are unchanged. Section 3's added O(|Df|) statement repeats the efficiency characterization already present in Appendix A; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a novel checkpoint-based unlearning method, competitive forgetting and utility, improved reference-model recovery and membership-inference performance, and effectiveness with earlier checkpoints. The rewritten contribution paragraph and softened novelty wording preserve these substantive claims.

C2.justification: v3 removes the conclusion's specific open research directions concerning temporal position, target frequency, long-range dependencies and cumulative exposure effects. Existing mechanism explanations, objective tradeoffs, checkpoint limitations and the pretraining-overlap caveat remain unchanged; the added main-text interpretations summarize Appendices F–H.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces the description of an anonymized supplementary code archive and its reproduction scripts with a brief GitHub availability statement. Both versions already provide the same repository link on page 1. Hardware and implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs establish a documentation change, not actual removal of resources.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix A's comparisons with Amnesiac Unlearning, Unrolling SGD and Rewind-to-Delete are unchanged. Section 3's new cross-reference summarizes existing positioning, and the additional main-text citation placements concern works already discussed in v2.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract and introduction, converts the numbered contributions into prose, adds main-text summaries of existing appendix investigations and adds acknowledgements. It also shortens the conclusion and reproducibility statement while retaining the overall section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised colors, legend, arrangement and caption. Main Tables 1–4 receive more compact formatting, and the appendix's v2 Table 10 becomes main-text Table 5, with corresponding renumbering. Other table labels and spacing receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 makes existing supplementary investigations easier to find and streamlines presentation. However, v2 Table 10 reports both ideal and MSAinstruct Accrecover as 0.45; v3 Table 5 raises the ideal to 0.98 while retaining MSAinstruct at 0.45 with a '+100%' annotation and near-ideal interpretation. The unexplained reference-score revisions and this new inconsistency complicate the comparison. Their effects alongside the presentation gains do not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
